title: Deuxième partie : variations sur l'équation des lacets [suite à La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois…, pages 293 à 650, dont table des matières] : notes et copies de notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Context: Grothendieck is studying algebraic groups attached to the 'équation des lacets' (loop relation). Here M_{ρ,σ} is an algebraic group of solutions attached to data ρ, σ, as in the previous pages. It carries two maps. The first is a character χ: M_{ρ,σ} → G_m. The second is a homomorphism Θ_G: M_{ρ,σ} → G, where G is a GL_2-type group with determinant δ_G. B'_0 is a subgroup of G (Borel-like). On the previous page, SM_{ρ,σ} was defined awkwardly as triples (x, u, f) with x ∈ M_{ρ,σ}, u ∈ B'_0, f ∈ SL_2, linked by a relation involving u and Θ_G(x).

On this page he simplifies ('Ouf !'). In (34) he takes as the new definition the fibre product of groups SM_{ρ,σ} := M_{ρ,σ} ×_{G_m} B'_0. Concretely, these are the pairs (x, u) with χ(x) = det(u), where δ_{B'_0} = δ_G restricted to B'_0. Being a fibre product of group homomorphisms, it is automatically a group scheme.

It then carries two extension structures. (35) Projection to M_{ρ,σ}: 1 → L_0 → SM → M → 1, with L_0 = Ker(det | B'_0). (36) Projection to B'_0: 1 → M^+_{ρ,σ} → SM → B'_0 → 1, with M^+ = Ker χ.

He then identifies the subgroup SM[0], corresponding to f = 1, i.e. u = Θ_G(x). That relation already forces det u = det Θ_G(x) = χ(x). So SM[0] is the graph of Θ_G restricted to M[0] = Θ_G^{-1}(B'_0), embedded by x ↦ (x, Θ_G(x)). It is therefore isomorphic to M[0] (formula 37).

On the next page, a splitting of (35) is shown to come from a splitting of 1 → L_0 → B'_0 → G_m → 1 (a torus section). This gives a semidirect product SM ≅ M ⋉ L_0, which Grothendieck finds less 'speaking' than (34) because it hides the canonical map to B'_0. This prepares 'Théorème bis': SM_{ρ,σ} is canonically isomorphic to the group of solutions (α, β, f) of the loop relations.
errors: Exactness on the right needs surjectivity hypotheses that are not stated. (35) is right-exact only if det: B'_0 → G_m is surjective (fppf). (36) is right-exact only if χ is surjective. Both are presumably true in context.
The embedding x ↦ (x, Θ_G(x)) landing in the fibre product uses the identity χ = δ_G∘Θ_G. This is asserted parenthetically ('qui implique déjà det U = det u') and presumably established earlier.

ideas.what: Define the auxiliary group SM as the fibre product M ×_{G_m} B'_0 of a character and a determinant
ideas.modern_name: fibre product (pullback) of algebraic groups; pullback of the extension 1 → L_0 → B'_0 → G_m → 1 along χ

ideas.what: Two exact sequences from the two projections of a fibre product, plus a semidirect decomposition via a torus splitting
Subgroup SM[0] identified with the graph of Θ_G on Θ_G^{-1}(B'_0)

deep.surprise_reason: The page is a routine (if clarifying) reformulation of an auxiliary group as a fibre product, with its two extension structures. The substantive content is the surrounding programme on loop-equation solution groups, not this page.
transcription_corrections: Top of page: '539' is the original page number of the notes; 472 is the archive scan number.
In (35) the map is x̃ = (x, u) ↦ x (u underlined), not (x, y). The sequence ends with '→ 1'.
In (36) the identification under M^+ reads M^+_{ρ,σ} = Ker(M_{ρ,σ} →χ G_m), and x̃ = (x, u) ↦ u.
'det U = det u' with det U = χ(x) is written under the line; 'U = Θ_G(x)' is likewise written under it.
'image isomorphique de M_{ρ,σ}[0] par (cf (14) p. 536) par x ↦ (x, Θ_G(x))': the insertion 'isomorphique' is written above the line, and a crossed-out 'x ↦ (' follows.
